title: Affinity-driven microbatch partitioner for attention-cost aware prefill/decode
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Current prefill/decode schedulers group requests by coarse heuristics (sequence length, priority buckets) which leads to suboptimal kernel choices and attention-layer hotspots. High-attention-cost requests (long contexts with wide heads) get interleaved with short low-cost requests, causing kernel thrashing, increased tail latency, and poor throughput for latency-sensitive tiers.

Goal: Implement an affinity-driven microbatch partitioner that groups in-flight prefill/decode phases into micro-slices based on a lightweight attention-cost fingerprint and kernel affinity score. The partitioner should: 1) reduce kernel selection churn, 2) preserve latency SLOs for P0/P1 traffic, and 3) improve overall GPU throughput by enabling larger homogeneous microbatches when safe.

Scope: This ticket covers design, runtime changes to the arbiter and allocator, offline simulator for affinity scoring, an end-to-end experiment on dedicated pools, and a staged rollout with canary metrics. Integration with KV cache accounting and fallback policies is included.

Non-goals: Full rework of decode hedging policies or long-term model-driven routing (future follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end implementation behind a feature flag. 2) Simulated scheduler shows >=5% throughput improvement or >=10% tail latency reduction for mixed workloads in the offline simulator. 3) Dedicated-pool canary demonstrates no regression in 99th percentile latency for P0 traffic and measurable cost/unit improvements. 4) Documentation and alerting added to Console per-route dashboard.
design_notes: Affinity fingerprint: 64-bit hash combining estimated attention FLOPs, seq_len, head_count, and quantization profile. Compute with a micro-cost estimator in O(1) per request.
Kernel affinity score: map fingerprint to preferred kernel family (fused-attn, multi-head-tiling, cuBLAS fallback) using a small LUT updated from runtime probes.
Microbatching window: opportunistic 5-25ms soft window; if latency budget for a request is near expiry, escalate to low-latency fastpath ignoring affinity grouping.
Fairness: credit-based aging where small/latency-sensitive requests get priority credits that allow skipping grouping for up to N windows. Credits replenish over time proportional to SLA tier.
Fallbacks: when affinity grouping would starve low-priority traffic, degrade to proportional fairness allocator. Also fall back to existing phase-splitter when LUT confidence is low.
Observability: emit per-window metrics: group_size, kernel_choice, avg_attention_cost, p50/p95/p99 latency, and kernel_switch_count.
Kernel probe: lightweight probe path to validate kernel throughput on a sampled subset of requests and update LUT with exponential moving average.
KV cache: ensure affinity grouping respects KV-cache locality—prefer grouping requests with compatible cache prefixes to avoid duplication of KV state transfers.
Safety flags: feature flag + per-pool cutoff to disable grouping for pools with <X GPUs or strict latency SLAs.
Open questions: best fingerprint composition for multi-modal models; how to integrate quantization profile changes in-flight.

updates: 2026-02-26: Kickoff sync — agreed on 64-bit affinity fingerprint and microbatch window defaults (5/15/25ms). Action: Aisha to write spec; Liam to start simulator scaffolding.
2026-03-02: Simulator prototype shows kernel_switch_count down 38% on mix of 20/80 long/short requests; throughput improved ~6% in median runs. Results attached to the design doc.

2026-03-05: Design review with Runtime team — Evan requested additional KV-cache locality constraint. Added to design_notes and tasks. Liam increased estimate for simulator to cover cache-aware sampling.
2026-03-08: Implemented early arbiter hooks to capture fingerprint; unit tests for fingerprint deterministic outputs added. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/512 (draft).

2026-03-10: Kernel probe micro-benchmarks show the LUT correctly prefers fused-attn for high attention FLOP fingerprints on A100; fallback correctly chosen for quantized kernels. Need larger sample coverage in canary.

2026-03-12: Canary plan finalized — dedicated-pool-canary will run 24h with mixed production-like traces. Monitoring queries and dashboards created in Console. Liam assigned to run canary and collect 24h metrics.
comments: Priya Nair (2026-03-03): Nice direction — small thought: consider head-wise attention sparsity signals (if available) for higher fidelity fingerprint. Might be noisy but could help kernel choice.
Evan Brooks (2026-03-05): KV locality is critical; if we group incompatible cache prefixes we'll blow memory and swap, causing regressions. Make locality a hard constraint in grouping.
Sofia Martinez (2026-03-07): Add unit test scenarios for credit starvation so we don't regress small-req latency when under sustained heavy long-request load.

Liam Chen (2026-03-09): Updated simulator config with cache-aware sampling and ran 50 randomized seeds; median improvement holds but variance increases at high head_count variance. Will tune credit replenishment.
Aisha Kapoor (2026-03-11): UX note — Console should show 'affinity grouping active' per-pool so operators can correlate regressions quickly. Added to Observability task.
